# @jpisgeek/fleet-status-monitoring

Fleet Status Monitoring combines two behavior types: a read-only adapter for
versioned system probes, and configurable health assessment with OS coverage,
freshness, evidence and a human-readable HTML snapshot. The included manual
workflow probes the serve host through native read-only OS APIs. An
authenticated existing-host handler supplies a bodyless named refresh action.

**Version** `2026.11.09.1` · **License** MIT · **Source**
https://github.com/jpisgeek/slog-bog/tree/main/fleet-status-monitoring

## Install

```
swamp extension pull @jpisgeek/fleet-status-monitoring
```

### Methods

#### `probe`

Observe the serve host through native read-only OS APIs; startup data disk only

No arguments.

#### `collect`

Collect local counters and normalize only results from the current fleet scan

No arguments.

### Data written

| resource       | lifetime | fields                                       | description                                                               |
| -------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `localProbe`   | 30d      | `startedAt`, `finishedAt`, `state`, `sample` | Native local observation; the workflow owns when it runs                  |
| `observations` | 30d      | `cycleId`, `checkedAt`, `systems`            | Per-system observations for one scan; failed attempts replace old success |

## Example

```yaml
# Collector: @jpisgeek/fleet-status-monitoring/system
globalArguments:
  targets:
    - id: local
      label: Mac Mini
      group: macos
      kind: physical
      collector: local
  cycleBehavior: fleet-health

# Report: @jpisgeek/fleet-status-monitoring
globalArguments:
  sourceBehavior: fleet-counters
  policy:
    maxAgeSeconds: 1800
    minMemoryPercent: 5
    minDiskPercent: 5
    minDiskBytes: 10737418240
    maxLoadPerCore: 2
  view:
    reportPath: /reports/fleet
    dashboardPath: /dashboard
    questPath: null
```

## Caveats

Follow QUICKSTART.md for server-backed setup and the unscheduled starter
workflow. HOSTING.md documents the optional handler for an existing HTTPS host;
pulling this package does not install a native dashboard page or start a server.
USE-CASES.md covers fleet monitoring and a Quest composition. The native local
probe supports macOS and Linux; Windows load and capacity remain explicitly
unavailable. An optional fixed Python probe supports restricted-command SSH
targets. The adapters themselves are platform independent. Remote targets
require a separately configured official @swamp/ssh behavior. Only one local
inventory target is allowed because it identifies the serve host. Runtime
retention is bounded and is not backup proof. Example fleets in USE-CASES.md are
generic compositions, not disclosures of a deployment.

## Security

This extension launches no subprocess and opens no network connection. Native
probes are explicit typed workflow actions; remote probes use the official SSH
behavior. It does not provision SSH keys, install agents, scan subnets or
perform remediation. The public package contains no deployment targets, keys,
grants or token files. Snapshot text is escaped; navigation stays same-origin;
optional Quest links are disabled by default. The existing host must authorize
every read and refresh, run only one fixed input-free workflow, and honor
request cancellation. No credentials are sent to the browser. Missing values
remain unknown, failed attempts cannot reuse old success, and only the startup
data filesystem is considered for disk alerts. Thresholds and coverage notes are
explicit inputs.

**Stored infrastructure data:** `observations` retains the declared machine
inventory, including SSH host names (`sourceHost`), labels and notes, along with
OS measurements and source evidence. It keeps at most 192 versions or 30 days.
The report's `state` and `fleet-report.html` omit `sourceHost` but include every
system's label, note, OS name and version, kernel, uptime, capacity and health.
Treat these artifacts as infrastructure data and authorize every viewer.

| File output                  | Content                                                       | Retention                      |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `html` (`fleet-report.html`) | Readable report and the full canonical state embedded as JSON | At most 12 versions or 30 days |

If separately deployed on an SSH target, the optional Python probe invokes fixed
read-only OS commands with a three-second timeout per command. It is not
executed by the extension or local starter. Stored HTML carries no HTTP headers
of its own; serve it through `createFleetHandler` or apply the same CSP, framing
restrictions, no-store and other response headers from HOSTING.md.

See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/jpisgeek/slog-bog/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
for the release gates every version passes before it reaches the registry.
